definition.name: ZOE
definition.component_state: For every exact canonical post-RFG component type T: omit T when n_T=0, emit O when n_T>0 is odd, and emit E when n_T>0 is even.

findings.statement: The minimal structurally motivated repair tested after the parity ceiling is the three-state ZOE count quotient: zero, positive odd, and positive even multiplicity.
Ungraded ZOE has zero mixed scalar-value classes on every tested transfer carrier and on both fresh holdouts.
On predeclared fresh 5x4-k4, ZOE is Q-V exact across 2,007,085 T2-O states while the exact-rank affine component-parity model has 16,550 contradictions.
ZOE is strictly coarser than full exact component multiplicity yet Q-V exact on 4x4-k4, 4x5-k4, and fresh 5x4-k4.
Adding rank mod 3 to ZOE is not required for scalar class purity on any tested carrier; in several carriers it refines the partition up to full multiplicity without changing Q-V exactness.
The parity failure is repaired by distinguishing zero multiplicity from positive-even multiplicity; the tested scalar quotient does not require exact positive-even magnitude.

narrowed_or_superseded: The earlier component-parity-plus-phase scalar picture is no longer the strongest count quotient: ungraded ZOE carries the tested scalar value information with a direct per-component count-state refinement.
Modulo 4 and modulo 6 remain passing finite controls but are not needed to express the currently smallest tested repair of the parity collision.
The two-syndrome search over binary component parity alone is superseded by a count-aware search surface.
nonclaims: ZOE is not proved minimal among all possible count quotients.
ZOE is not proved universally sufficient.
ZOE does not establish Q-A or Q-F sufficiency.
next_question: Can exact component identity now be compressed structurally by aggregating ZOE counts over frozen frontier-relative descriptors such as TOPO_RPAR or REL_INC without reintroducing scalar collisions?
